Houston County Commissioners Meeting
                              October 6, 2026
                              Perry, Georgia
The Houston County Board of Commissioners met in a Regular Session at 9:00 a.m. on
Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at the Houston County Courthouse in Perry, Georgia. Chairman
Perdue presided, and Commissioners Byrd, Gottwals, Robinson, and Talton were present.
Director of Administration Robbie Dunbar, Director of Operations Brian Jones, and County
Attorney Tom Hall were also present.

Commissioner Talton gave the invocation.

Commissioner Byrd led those in attendance in the Pledge of Allegiance.

Col. Johari Hemphill, Commander of the 78th Air Base Wing, spoke about his 27 years of
service in the Air Force. Col. Hemphill then spoke about the approximately 20,000 personnel
who work at Robins Air Force Base and discussed the three focus areas he has sought to
implement as Commander: mission readiness, base culture, and community partnerships. He
mentioned the April 17–18, 2027, air show at Robins Air Force Base, and spoke about his
family. He concluded by saying that he greatly appreciates and is impressed by the community
support for Robins Air Force Base from Houston County and Middle Georgia. Col. Hemphill
was accompanied to the meeting by Chief MSgt. Morales.

Chairman Perdue, and each Commissioner, expressed appreciation to Col. Hemphill for his
service, his partnership with the Houston County community, and his leadership at the Base.
Mr. Gottwals specifically mentioned a quote from George Orwell: “People sleep peaceably in
their beds at night only because rough men stand ready to do violence on their behalf.”

Judith Malone, Library Director for the Houston County Public Libraries, gave the FY2026
annual report of activities, services, and programs offered by the library system over the course
of the previous fiscal year.

Chairman Perdue, and each Commissioner, thanked Ms. Malone for her service, leadership, and
commitment to the citizens of Houston County through her direction of the County’s library
system.

Chairman Perdue explained to those present that the second reading of the alcohol license for
Rock N Roll Liquors would not occur at today’s meeting due to an error by the applicant in
placing the required notice in the newspaper. He stated that the alcohol license would be heard
at the October 20 Commissioners meeting.

Chairman Perdue requested a motion to add an item to the agenda for an Executive Session.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to add item #17, an
Executive Session for Attorney Client consultation as provided in O.C.G.A. § 50-14-2(1).

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
meeting minutes from the September 22, 2026, Board meeting.

Chief Building Inspector Tim Andrews presented Special Exception Applications numbers
2955, 2958, 2966, 2968, 2969, 2970, 2971, and 2973.

County Attorney Tom Hall made a blanket statement for the benefit of all applicants for Special
Exceptions for home occupations: even if the Board of Commissioners approves an application,
neighborhood covenants may still impose certain restrictions upon or against home businesses.
These restrictive covenants are not superseded by any action taken by the Board of
Commissioners. The actions taken by the Board will not change any provision within the
covenant that prohibits any commercial or business activity.



                Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 9

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 8


Chairman Perdue closed the regular portion of the meeting and opened a Public Hearing.

Applicant #2955 was present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2958 was not present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2966 was not present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2968 was present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2969 was present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2970 was present; there was no opposition.
Applicant #2971 was present and gave additional information about her nonprofit; there was no
opposition.
Applicant #2973 was present; there was no opposition.

There being no further comments Chairman Perdue closed the Public Hearing and reopened the
regular portion of the meeting.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
following Special Exception Applications to include any and all stipulations as noted on the
Zoning & Appeals recommendation and Section 95 Requirements staff report:

#2955           Wanda Scott                  Crafts & Writing
#2968           Landon Howe                  Landscaping
#2969           George & Jennifer Yakush     Bread & Desserts Baking
#2970           Kenneth & Karen Hicks        Ballroom Dancing
#2971           Patricia Prime               Motherhood Support & Comm. Education
                                             Non-Profit
#2973           Charles & Angela Hebenstreit Transport

Also, to deny Special Exception Application #2958 submitted by Blake Horne and table Special
Exception Application #2966 submitted by Charles Dagley.

Mr. Andrews informed the approved business license applicants that the next step in obtaining
their business license was to apply at the Commissioner’s Office.

Mr. Byrd presented a request to replace the servers, storage, and network infrastructure
supporting the County’s Court Management software and related judicial systems.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve Quote
Q-44362 from The Redesign Group, of El Segundo, California, in the amount of $427,644.80
for the replacement of the servers, storage, and network infrastructure supporting the County’s
Court Management software and related judicial systems.

Mr. Gottwals stated that this purchase would be funded by the 2018 SPLOST.

Ms. Robinson commented that the software changeover in 2019 was very difficult.

Chairman Perdue commented that this purchase is for a change and upgrade in hardware only,
not software, and that he also remembers the painful and difficult software changeover that
Commissioner Robinson spoke of in the judicial software program.

Mr. Byrd presented a request to correct a motion amount on the 2026 LMIG Road Project
approved at the April 21, 2026, Board meeting.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to approve
correcting the amount of the contract stated in the motion approving the 2026 LMIG Road
Project changing the amount from $2,948,046.76 to $2,948,167.75. No correction is needed on
the contract signed with Reames and Son Construction.


               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 10

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 9


Chairman Perdue thanked County Administrative and Accounting personnel for catching this
error.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Ms. Robinson, to approve the reappointment of the following
to the Central Georgia Joint Development Authority for a term of July 6, 2026, through July 6,
2030:

    •   Dan Perdue
    •   Tommy Stalnaker
    •   Rob Brooks

Mr. Byrd thanked those nominated for their willingness to serve.

Chairman Perdue noted that the Central Georgia Joint Development Authority comprises 11
counties and focuses primarily on supporting Robins Air Force Base. He cited purchases of
properties north of the Base in the crash zone and, in Houston County, west of Hwy. 247 in the
noise contour zone. The Department of Defense had identified these properties as problems for
the Base.

Ms. Robinson presented a request to enter into an Intergovernmental Agreement with the City
of Centerville that will replace the prior infrastructure agreement.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve
entering into an Infrastructure Agreement with the City of Centerville establishing updated
standards for transition meters, County infrastructure, and water connection fees.

Chairman Perdue thanked City of Centerville officials for working with the County on this
agreement.

Ms. Robinson presented a request to enter into an agreement for the design of a detention pond
at the HEMA Warehouse.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve
entering into a service agreement with Axis Engineering Consultants, LLC, of Warner Robins,
Georgia, in the amount of $14,750, for the design of a detention pond to provide stormwater
management for the HEMA Warehouse. This work will be funded by the General Fund and has
a timeline of three months from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed.

Ms. Robinson presented a request to approve a proposal to upgrade the fuel pumps, the fuel
management units, and software at the Warner Robins and Perry fuel stations.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
proposal from MECO/Gasboy-EKOS, of Macon, Georgia, with a total turnkey cost of
$281,358.40, and a recurring annual software cost of $6,336 after the first year, and an optional
warranty and maintenance coverage for years 2-5 is available at an annual cost of $9,470. This
upgrade, with an eight-week completion timeline, will be funded by 2018 SPLOST.

Chairman Perdue thanked Purchasing Department staff for their help with this action and
commented on the reliability issues with the current pumps and how those issues could become
serious for Sheriff’s Office staff attempting to refuel if the pumps were unavailable. He stated
that this would be a complete replacement of the pumps and fueling system with built-in fraud
and theft prevention systems.

Ms. Robinson presented a request from the City of Warner Robins for approval of a
Memorandum of Understanding that divides the 2026 Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) funds
equally between the Warner Robins Police Department and the Houston County Sheriff's Office.




               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 11

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 10



Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to approve
entering a Memorandum of Understanding with the City of Warner Robins and the Warner
Robins Police Department for the division of the 2026 Justice Assistance Grant O-BJA-2026-
172705, with $31,946 allocated to the Houston County Sheriff's Office and $31,946 to the
Warner Robins Police Department. The City of Warner Robins will serve as fiscal agent for the
joint funds.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request for approval of an amendment to the Ingress and Egress
Easement Agreement between the Houston County Board of Commissioners, and the Hospital
Authority of Houston County.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
signing of an Amendment to Ingress and Egress Easement Agreement originally dated
December 10, 2025, recorded in Deed Book 10757, Pages 779-783, Clerk’s Office, Houston
County Superior Court.

Chairman Perdue thanked Emory Healthcare and the Houston County Hospital Authority for
their cooperation.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request to fill the vacant Assistant District Attorney position at the
District Attorney's Office.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
the hiring of Mr. Brian E. Brupbacher for the position of Assistant District Attorney at a Grade
30, Step E effective October 7, 2026. Personnel has reviewed his qualifications and confirms
that he meets the criteria for the E Step.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request to fill the vacant Senior Assistant Public Defender position at
the Public Defender's Office.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
the hiring of Ms. Lela Acker to fill the vacant Senior Assistant Public Defender position at a
Grade 34, Step C, effective October 7, 2026. Personnel has reviewed Ms. Acker's qualifications
and confirms that she meets the criteria.

Chairman Perdue thanked Sara Myers, Houston County Public Defender, for attending and
thanked Ms. Myers for her work. He also stated that he was glad to see Ms. Acker joining the
team.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request for revisions to the Appeals Policy of the Houston County
Personnel Manual.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve
revisions to Articles V, VI, X, XI, XII, XIII, and XV of the Houston County Personnel Manual
effective October 7, 2026. These revisions will establish two consistent employee review
processes, align policies with the revised disciplinary and grievance procedures, and update the
related administrative provisions.

Chairman Perdue explained that Articles X and XI received the primary updates and that
changes in other articles were made to properly reference the changes in Articles X and XI. He
also said these changes focused on engaging a third party to hear employee appeals.

Mr. Talton presented a request for approval of an Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with the
City of Perry that sets the conditions under which the County will provide emergency fuel
assistance to the City of Perry.



               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 12

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 11



Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to
approve the renewal of the Intergovernmental Agreement for the emergency use of the County
fuel supply to the City of Perry. This renewal will expire on October 20, 2028.

Chairman Perdue stated that he is happy this agreement has not been used in the last two years
it has been in effect. He stated that it was important to have a backup fuel source in case of a
natural or man-made disaster. He also recognized Purchasing Department staff for making sure
the County’s fuel tanks were full ahead of an impending weather-related situation, such as a
hurricane or winter storm.

Mr. Talton presented a request for approval of a bid on a truck for use in the Patrol Division of
the Sheriff's Office.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the bid
from Countryside Chevrolet, of Byron, Georgia for the purchase of one 2026 Chevrolet
Silverado in the amount of $54,852.49, for use in the Patrol Division. This purchase will be
funded by 2024 SPLOST.

Mr. Talton presented a request for approval of a bid on a truck for the Warrants Division of the
Sheriff's Office.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the bid
from Brannen Motors of Unadilla, Georgia, in the amount of $49,980, for a 2024 one-half ton
Police Pursuit Vehicle pickup truck. This purchase will be reimbursed by the Sheriff's Office
Drug Account.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
payment of the bills totaling $3,708,274.25.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Talton and carried unanimously by all to enter into an
Executive Session for Attorney Client consultation as provided in O.C.G.A. § 50-14-2(1).

After exiting the Executive Session Chairman Perdue reconvened the meeting.

Chairman Perdue opened the floor for Commissioner Comments.

Ms. Robinson thanked everyone for attending and commented on the bigger and better things
occurring in Houston County. She also expressed her condolences to the communities affected
by the recent mass shootings.

Mr. Byrd commented on the upcoming Georgia National Fair and encouraged everyone to visit
and enjoy it. He mentioned the Sheriff Cullen Talton Memorial Golf Tournament and the funds
raised in support of the Georgia Sheriffs’ Youth Homes. He thanked Sheriff Moulton for
continuing this event.

Commissioner Talton expressed his excitement about all the positive things happening in
Houston County and said he was happy to serve, live, and work in Houston County.

Commissioner Gottwals commented on the great meeting, stating that with the military, the
Fair, new businesses starting up, new developments, and the outstanding library system, there
were great things happening in Houston County.




               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 13

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 12



Chairman Perdue commented on the good work that took place during the meeting and thanked
the Commissioners and staff for their involvement. He asked everyone to pray for the
surrounding communities recently suffering from violence and expressed appreciation for the
Sheriff’s Office being willing to assist surrounding counties when needed. He concluded his
comments by stating that the Georgia National Fair was coming up and encouraged everyone to
enjoy and attend the Fair.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
adjourning the meeting. Meeting adjourned.
